text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Deputy Prime Minister Nguyen Khanh, speaking during a visit by a delegation of China's Union of Scientists and Technologists Associations, said Vietnam was determined to develop the national economy by boosting scientific and technological research.
-- The Vietnam-Thailand Joint Finance Commission held its first two-day session in Hanoi last week to promote bilateral cooperation.

-- Foreign bank branches, representative offices and joint-venture banks should improve their operating capacity and maximise existing potential next year, a report from the central State Bank of Vietnam says. It says foreign banks should pay more attention to financing projects, extending medium- and long-term credit as well as supporting Vietnamese economic organisations in terms of capital.

-- Vietnam should look to alternative energy sources rather than become too reliant on hydro-power, two experts write in a report. They urge the development of gas turbine plants in southern provinces to provide electricity for central Vietnam and even for the north in case of emergency.
-- A new campaign on maintaining social order and security has been launched in Hanoi ahead of the traditional Tet Lunar New Year.
-- 10,000 hectares of paddy field have been inundated following last week's torrential rain in the coastal province of Binh Dinh.
-- Crude oil output from the White Tiger and Big Bear fields between January 1 and December 22 was 8.46 million tonnes.

-- Chairman of the Ho Chi Minh City People's Council Pham Chanh Truc, in a Christmas-time message, called on the country's Christians to make more of a contribution to the country's socio-economic development.
